## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass over the board's task card in every state it can show, plus long titles, many labels, unbroken titles and missing fields. Each state is a fixture rendered through the real `TaskCard` component in headless WebKit at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The pass found three real overflows, all at the 220 px laptop card width, and I fixed them in the component and stylesheet. The new suite has 35 cases and passes; the related card and board suites (28 files, 243 tests) pass; the scoped `repoos check` is green. The QA doc is at `docs/qa/2026-11-task-cards-states-qa.md`.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for every card state at three widths, with no overlap or clipping, driven headless against fixtures only. I did not drive a live server. Instead I mount `TaskCard` in jsdom for each fixture, capture its markup, and render that markup in WebKit with the built global stylesheet and the scoped CSS of `CopyableNumber`, the one child component whose scoped styles the card relies on. The existing `work-board-moves-qa-browser.test.ts` set the pattern, so I copied its harness rather than inventing one.

The check has two rules that run on every render. First, no spill: the card is `overflow: hidden`, so a child that runs past the card edge is clipped without any visible sign. Every visible descendant must sit inside the card's box. Second, no placeholder text: a missing field must not print `undefined`, `null`, `NaN` or `[object Object]`. A viewport check also confirms the card stays on screen and the document doesn't widen.

Card widths are representative. The board shares the viewport across its columns, so I used 351 px for a phone, 336 px for a tablet and 220 px for a laptop, where five columns share the width. The laptop width is the stress case. I stated this assumption in the doc rather than measuring a live board.

Archived tasks do not reach a card. The store filters `isArchived` out of every column and keeps them in `archivedTasks`, so I asserted that in jsdom rather than rendering a card.

## Approaches tried

I first wrote the suite with placeholder assertions and then replaced them. The archived test originally called a getter I had guessed at; I checked the store and used `byStatus(...)` and `archivedTasks` instead. My first paused-state test checked nothing, so I replaced it with a real assertion on the stalled badge.

I tried running the new file with bare `bunx vitest`, which failed because that config doesn't load the Vue plugin. The repo's `bun run test:vitest` wrapper uses `src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`, and that works.

For the header fix I considered truncating the whole header group and also letting it wrap. Truncation hides the agent button or the priority badge, which carry information, so I made the header row wrap and truncated only the type chip. For the type chip I used a styled `data-tip` for the full name instead of a native `title`, which the repo's UI conventions forbid in new UI.

## Challenges and blockers

The first run failed three of its 35 cases, all at 1280 px. Each was a real overflow: a long type name, a long human handle, and a `needs merge` badge combined with the header's fixed row. The 375 and 768 widths passed, which is why a single-width check would have missed them. The fix needed a rebuild of the UI, since the WebKit harness reads the built global stylesheet and not source; I rebuilt with `bun run build:ui` before rerunning.

Fixing the header broke one existing test, `task-card-agent-header.test.ts`, which found the header row by its old `gap-[7px]` class. The test asserted the implementation's class name, not behaviour, so I updated the selector to the new `flex-wrap` anchor. I did not weaken the assertion.

The scoped `repoos check` step for tests was reported as skipped by the environment (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`), so the changed-path test run did not execute in this session. I ran the related suites directly and they pass. RepoOS's server-side verification will run its own suite.

## Key learnings

A card-width check has to use the width the board really gives it. Checking only the phone width missed the laptop regressions entirely, and the narrow five-column case is where header and chip content collide.

Using `overflow: hidden` on a card makes spills silent. An overflow check that only looks at the viewport would pass a clipped chip, so the test measures descendants against the card's own box.

For a header row that holds several fixed-size badges, letting the row wrap is safer than truncating the group. The truncation should go on the one element whose text can vary in length, the type chip, and the full value should be reachable through the styled tooltip.

Screenshots are the cheapest check on a layout fix. I captured full-page JPEGs for every fixture and width into the ignored `.repoos/qa-evidence/1246/`, and I looked at the narrow many-labels, needs-input and needs-merge cards before trusting the numbers.

Not covered here: board columns with extreme labels, child components' scoped styles beyond `CopyableNumber`, and real-device touch or font metrics. The doc's limits section lists them, and they are the obvious next checks if the board shows a regression.
